name: Switzerland

facts.religion: Catholic about 32%, Reformed Protestant about 20%, no religion about 34%

system_note: A directorial system: a seven-member Federal Council governs collectively.
snapshot: A rich, neutral federation run by consensus and direct democracy, which struck a deal in 2025 to cut punishing US tariffs on its exports.
culture: Switzerland has four national languages: German, French, Italian and Romansh. Citizens vote several times a year in referendums on everything from taxes to cow horns. Chocolate, cheese, watches and Alpine skiing are national icons, and Geneva hosts many UN agencies and the Red Cross.
society: Switzerland is among the world's richest countries, with pharma giants like Roche and Novartis, banking and precision industry. It remains outside the EU but tied to it by bilateral treaties. Neutrality has been tested by sanctions on Russia. Glacier loss from climate change is visible across the Alps.
situation: The seven-member Federal Council is shared among the four largest parties, and Guy Parmelin of the Swiss People's Party holds the rotating presidency in 2026. In 2025 the US imposed a 39 percent tariff on Swiss goods before a deal lowered it. On 14 June 2026 voters rejected, by about 55 percent, the Swiss People's Party's initiative to cap the population at 10 million, which would have endangered free movement with the EU as a new package of EU treaties heads toward a national vote.
power: A federal directorial republic. Parliament elects a seven-member Federal Council that governs collectively; the cantons are powerful, and citizens can force national referendums on almost any law.

leaders.state: Federal Council, with Guy Parmelin as President of the Confederation for 2026

sources.label: Anadolu: voters reject the population cap
